chapter: Tuba, brass bands and the road
title: Road trips with Sam Morgan and the packing house job
summary: He toured Gulf Coast towns with Sam Morgan, tired of the road, and in 1928 took a packing house job he held about twenty years while recording.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Just get up a band. Just say, well we'll get up a bunch of fellas and make bands. See, no name. Yeah. Well, that was it. And it went a little further. And the road got so bad of playing on the road. Going out. Making night here and night there and the night next place. That was with Sam Morgan band, you name it? Yeah. Well, we used to go, when I was with Sam Morgan band, we used to go Pensacola, Mobile, Bloxy, Gulfport, and Hattiesbury. Then we'd come on back in town, you see? Mm-hmm. And we'd have a Saturday night play and Sunday night play and a Monday night play. Then we'd go on the road around like Tuesday. Tuesday. Tuesday. Oh, maybe. Yeah. Yeah. Well, it went around like that for a while and I got tired playing. I got tired of the road and I went back to work in the packing house for lodging on Collins. By what year would that be? That would be in 28.
What did you pack? What kind of a place? Packing house. Oh, meat? Yeah, meat house.

Which one was it? Hmm? Which one? Longinor and Collins. That's a local house, you know. Oh, I see. Did you still land? Oh, they did. The old man died. Longinor died and then old man Collins died right maybe a year or so behind, you see. And then I got in bad luck. I had to quit working in the packing house because I got crippled. About how long were you there? How long I worked there? Oh, about 20 years. In the packing house. That's all. I made records with you and I was working there. Working there. I didn't know where you were working. At the same time. I didn't know. See. And well, when I was making records with you, I'd be maybe get off that night that I'd make records for you early for the night and then maybe go back there around 12, 1 o'clock. See?
Well, you were still playing music right now while you worked there. While I was working for Bill. But otherwise, I mean, you were playing, you even played parades in those days too.
